data.name: Eilshan
data.gender_notes: Eilshan is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Islamic tradition, Eilshan is believed to be derived from the Arabic word 'ilah' meaning 'God'. The name signifies being born from or belonging to God, emphasizing the divine origin of the individual. The name Eilshan carries the meaning “Born from God” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Eilshan usually hope their child will grow to embody born from god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Eilshan belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Born from God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Eilshan total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

historical_references.reference: Ibn Battuta's travels mention a city called Eilshan in present-day Kazakhstan. He visited the city around 1333 CE during the Chagatai Khanate period.
historical_references.context: Ibn Battuta was a Moroccan traveler who explored Asia extensively. He visited Eilshan, which was then an important city in the Chagatai Khanate, and wrote about it in his travelogues.

historical_references.reference: Al-Idrisi, a Geographer from Seville, Spain, mentions a city called Eilshan in the 12th century CE in his work 'Nuzhat al-mushtaq fi ikhtiraq al-afaq'. He describes it as a prosperous city in the region of Mawarannahr (Transoxania).
historical_references.context: Al-Idrisi was a geographer and cartographer who wrote a comprehensive description of the world as known to the Muslims at that time. He mentions Eilshan as a prosperous city in the region of Mawarannahr, which was then under the control of the Karakhanid Empire.
